    Temporal statistics of per-frame MSSR maps

    Source: R/temporal.R
    mssr_temporal.Rd

    Computes single-frame MSSR (mssr()) for every frame of an image sequence and reduces the stack of maps pixel by pixel with one temporal statistic, as in the temporal MSSR (t-MSSR) of Torres-Garcia et al. (2022, Fig. 7a and Supplementary Note 5.2). The output is a temporal statistic of nonlinear structure maps: it is not a quantitative intensity, and no gain in resolution is implied (see Interpretation). mssr_stack() stores the per-frame maps so that several statistics can be computed without recomputing MSSR.

    Usage

    mssr_temporal(
  x,
  statistic,
  fwhm,
  amp = 1L,
  order = 1L,
  intensity_normalize = TRUE,
  mesh = TRUE,
  grid = c("extent", "endpoint"),
  kernel = c("disk", "square"),
  rounding = c("half_even", "half_up"),
  frames = NULL,
  sign = c("signed", "absolute"),
  background = NULL,
  max_output_pixels = 5e+07,
  max_memory_bytes = NULL
)

mssr_stack(
  x,
  fwhm,
  amp = 1L,
  order = 1L,
  intensity_normalize = TRUE,
  mesh = TRUE,
  grid = c("extent", "endpoint"),
  kernel = c("disk", "square"),
  rounding = c("half_even", "half_up"),
  frames = NULL,
  max_output_pixels = 5e+07,
  max_memory_bytes = NULL
)

    Arguments

    x

    Either a plain numeric array with dimensions rows x columns x frames (rows = y, columns = x) and finite values, or an mssr_stack from mssr_stack(). For an mssr_stack, the per-frame arguments (fwhm to rounding and max_output_pixels) must not be given; the stored maps already fix them.

    statistic

    One of "mean", "var", "tpm", "cv", "sofi2", "sofi3" or "sofi4". Required: none of them is a safe default.

    fwhm, amp, order, intensity_normalize, mesh, grid, kernel, rounding, max_output_pixels

    Per-frame MSSR settings, exactly as in mssr(). fwhm is required for raw frames.

    frames

    Optional contiguous, increasing frame indices; the lags need consecutive frames. Defaults to all frames.

    sign

    For "sofi2", "sofi3" and "sofi4": "signed" (default) returns the cumulant, "absolute" its absolute value. Other statistics accept only "signed".

    background

    Optional logical matrix on the input grid that marks signal-free pixels for diagnostics$mesh_index. By default these are the pixels whose raw temporal mean is below the median of that mean. Because the mesh index is formed only with amp > 1 on the extent grid, giving background otherwise is an error.

    max_memory_bytes

    Optional positive allocation-estimate budget (see Computation). This is not a hard process-memory cap. For an mssr_stack, whose maps already exist, it limits the reduction's buffers.

    Value

    mssr_temporal() returns an mssr_result (result schema 1.1.0) with role "temporal_<statistic>", values on the amplified grid and the same transform as mssr(). parameters holds the per-frame MSSR settings plus statistic, frames (the number of frames used), first_frame (the first frame's index in the original input), sign ("not_applicable" for statistics other than SOFI) and definition. diagnostics counts degenerate_frames, warning_frames and order_steps_skipped over the frames, and gives zero_fraction, negative_fraction, mesh_index, mesh_region, trend and the computation path. mssr_stack() returns an object of class mssr_stack: values (an array of the per-frame maps), transform, parameters (with frames and first_frame), engine, diagnostics (a data frame with one row per frame, including the raw frame's mean input_mean) and input_mean (the raw temporal mean on the input grid).

    diagnostics$mesh_index measures the sub-pixel grid on signal-free input pixels only, because where structure is present the index mixes structure and grid. Each such input pixel contributes its whole amp x amp block of output pixels; the index is the range of the mean over the amp x amp sub-pixel phases, divided by the absolute mean of these blocks. For the SOFI statistics it is computed on the absolute values, because signed cumulants average to about zero where there is no signal. It is formed only on the default grid = "extent", where every input pixel holds each phase exactly once; on the endpoint grid the phases drift across the field.

    mesh_region names the pixels used: "below_median", the pixels whose raw temporal mean over the selected frames lies strictly below its median; "below_median_stack", the same rule for a frame subset of an mssr_stack, whose stored raw mean covers all of its frames, so the index can differ from that of the raw frames; "background", a supplied mask; or "not_computed" for amp = 1 and the endpoint grid. mesh_pixels counts the input pixels used. mesh_index is NULL when no index is computed, when no pixel qualifies (for example when more than half of the pixels share the lowest raw mean, so that none lies below the median; supply background then), or when the mean of the blocks is 0.

    diagnostics$trend is the mean of the raw frames over the whole field in the last tenth of the selected frames divided by that in the first tenth (at least one frame each); NULL when the first is 0. It is reported for every statistic and corrects nothing.

    Details

    Definitions. Per output pixel, x_1, ..., x_M are the values of the M selected frames' MSSR maps, m is their mean and d_t = x_t - m. Following Supplementary Table S2:

    statisticValueMinimum M
    "mean"m1
    "var"(1/M) sum(d_t^2)2
    "tpm"(sum(x_t))^21
    "cv"var / m, and 0 where m = 02
    "sofi2"(1/(M-1)) sum_{t=1}^{M-1} d_t d_{t+1}2
    "sofi3"(1/(M-2)) sum_{t=1}^{M-2} d_t d_{t+1} d_{t+2}3
    "sofi4"A(0,1,2,3) - A(0,1)A(2,3) - A(0,2)A(1,3) - A(0,3)A(1,2)4

    For "sofi4", A(L) is the average over t = 1, ..., M - 3 of the product of d_{t+l} for the lags l in L; all its terms use the same frames.

    • "var" is the population variance; the sample variance is larger by M / (M - 1).

    • "tpm" equals M^2 * mean^2. For non-negative maps it is a monotone function of the mean and shows nothing that "mean" does not; it is offered because every implementation by the authors computes it.

    • "cv" is the supplement's "CV", literally Var / Mean: an index of dispersion, not the standard deviation divided by the mean. It takes the sign of the mean, so it is negative where the mean is negative (signed input). It is 0 where the mean, formed in the scaled range described under Computation, is exactly 0; where the mean is tiny compared with the variance the ratio becomes very large, and a ratio beyond the numeric range is refused.

    • "sofi2" to "sofi4" are lagged auto-cumulants of signed deviations. Noise that is independent from frame to frame does not enter their expectation. Orders 3 and 4 change sign with the emitters' duty cycle, so displays usually need sign = "absolute".

    The "SOFI" outputs of the authors' Python, MATLAB and Fiji tools are other statistics, so they do not match these values by design. The Python and MATLAB tools use absolute deviations at zero lag, which makes their order 2 the variance without the first frame. The Fiji plugin uses absolute deviations with lags that wrap around the ends of the acquisition. Their variance divides by M - 1 except in the Python tool. See vignette("method-concordance").

    Interpretation. "var", "cv" and the SOFI statistics depend on how the emitters blink and on the noise, and every map is a nonlinear function of its frame. Treat the outputs as visual aids:

    • Variance, "cv" and SOFI of per-frame MSSR maps, and higher MSSR orders, can show two maxima where there is a single emitter.

    • When emitters are rarely on and dim, MSSR of nearly empty frames adds maxima to every statistic.

    • With amp > 1, signal-free regions show a sub-pixel grid with the period amp; diagnostics$mesh_index reports its size there (see Value).

    • The article recommends Fourier interpolation for temporal analysis. The package amplifies with the supplement's cubic kernel and mesh compensation instead; Fourier interpolation is not implemented.

    No drift, bleaching or background correction is applied. "var", "cv" and the SOFI statistics treat slow intensity trends (bleaching, drift, focus changes) as fluctuation, so a large trend inflates them. Correct the frames first, and record what was done; diagnostics$trend reports the ratio of the raw intensity at the end and at the start of the selected frames.

    Computation. Every statistic is formed from centered deviations in frame order, in a power-of-two scaled range so that products of up to four deviations stay representable. The scaling is undone at the end; a value that would exceed the numeric range, or a nonzero value that would fall below the smallest representable magnitude, raises mssrscopR_error_numerical, and very small results keep only subnormal precision. "mean" and "tpm" need one pass over the frames. The others need the mean first and then a second pass. The per-frame maps are stored for it when they fit (diagnostics$path "stored"), else every frame's MSSR is computed again ("recompute"), which doubles the time. Both paths give the same values. With max_memory_bytes = NULL the maps are stored when they take at most 2 GiB, counted with the estimate's 100 percent margin for stored maps; with a budget, they are stored when the estimate fits it, and a call whose recompute path does not fit is refused. mssr_estimate_resources() reports both estimates; they are checked before any frame is read. The input array is read one frame at a time and never copied as a whole. mssr_stack() stores every map: without max_memory_bytes it refuses (with mssrscopR_error_resource) maps that would take more than 2 GiB with that margin.

    Each frame must satisfy the checks of mssr(); errors name the frame. Warnings of the frames' mssr() calls (negative values, skipped refinement steps) are collected and given once per class, with the number of frames concerned. A call-level mssrscopR_warning_unqualified_order is given for orders above 3.

    References

    Torres-Garcia E, Pinto-Camara R, Linares A, et al. Extending resolution within a single imaging frame. Nature Communications 2022;13:7452. doi:10.1038/s41467-022-34693-9

    Dertinger T, Colyer R, Iyer G, Weiss S, Enderlein J. Fast, background-free, 3D super-resolution optical fluctuation imaging (SOFI). PNAS 2009;106:22287-22292. doi:10.1073/pnas.0907866106

    See also

    mssr(), mssr_estimate_resources(), vignette("temporal")

    Examples

    # Two blinking emitters, 40 frames, Poisson noise (synthetic).
set.seed(1)
g <- expand.grid(r = 1:16, c = 1:16)
spot <- function(r0, c0) exp(-((g$r - r0)^2 + (g$c - c0)^2) / (2 * (3 / 2.3548)^2))
x <- array(0, c(16, 16, 40))
for (t in 1:40) {
  on <- stats::runif(2) < 0.4
  x[, , t] <- stats::rpois(256, 20 * (on[1] * spot(8, 7) + on[2] * spot(8, 10)) + 2)
}
s <- mssr_stack(x, fwhm = 3)
v <- mssr_temporal(s, "var")
v
#> <mssr_result> temporal_var
#>   input 16 x 16 -> output 16 x 16 (amp 1, extent grid)
#>   var of 40 frame(s) (frames 1 to 40)
#>   per frame: fwhm 3 px, order 1, kernel disk (half-size 2)
#>   0 degenerate frame(s), 0 frame(s) with warnings; path stack
#>   trend (last / first tenth of frames) 0.997; no mesh index (amp 1 or endpoint grid)
#>   Temporal statistic of nonlinear structure maps, not a quantitative intensity.
m <- mssr_temporal(s, "mean")
all.equal(mssr_temporal(s, "tpm")$values, 40^2 * m$values^2)
#> [1] TRUE
